text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 20 in history.
1616 - Thomas Bartholin born. Danish physician and mathematician who, in 1652, became the first to describe fully the human lymphatic system.
1632 - Sir Christopher Wren born. English architect and astronomer. Designed and built over 50 churches in London, most notably St Paul's Cathedral.
1740 - Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor and pretender to the throne of Spain, died.
1784 - Lord Palmerston, British statesman, born as Henry John Temple. He was prime minister twice between 1855 and 1865.
1818 - By agreement between the United States and Britain, the U.S.-Canada border was set at the 49th parallel, with a joint occupation of Oregon for 10 years.
1827 - In the Greek War of Independence, the Turkish and Egyptian fleets were destroyed by the British, French and Russians at the Battle of Navarino.
1854 - (Jean-Nicolas) Arthur Rimbaud born. Imaginative French poet who was a great influence on the Symbolist movement.
1884 - Bela Lugosi, Hungarian actor in horror films, born as Bela Blasko. As well as his Frankenstein films, he also appeared in "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "Dracula".
1891 - Sir James Chadwick born. British physicist who won the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1935 for his discovery of the neutron.
1891 - Dame Anna Neagle, British actress in films and musicals, born as Marjorie Robertson.
1918 - In the third of an exchange of notes between U.S. President Woodrow Wilson and the Germans aimed at an armistice, the Germans agreed to further concessions.

1935 - Mao Zedong and his Communist forces ended their "Long March" at Yan'an, in Shaanxi, northwest China, one year after beginning their epic flight from Chiang Kai-shek's Kuomintang armies in the southeast.
1944 - In World War Two, Russian and Yugoslav forces captured Belgrade.
1960 - The trial started in London of Penguin Books, charged with contravening Britain's Obscene Publications Act by publishing D.H. Lawrence's novel "Lady Chatterley's Lover".
1964 - Herbert Hoover, who served as 31st president of the United States 1929-33, died.
1971 - West German Chancellor Willy Brandt was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
1973 - In Australia, Queen Elizabeth II officially opened the Sydney Opera House.
1986 - In Israel, Likud party leader Yitzhak Shamir took over as prime minister from Labour's Shimon Peres under a 1984 power-sharing arrangement.
1989 - Sir Anthony Quayle, English actor best remembered for his roles in "Lawrence of Arabia", "Ice Cold in Alex" and "The Guns of Navarone", died of cancer.
1994 - A landmine explosion killed Tajikistan's deputy prime minister, casting a shadow over the first day of a ceasefire between the ex-communist government and the Afghanistan-based opposition.
1995 - Willy Claes resigned as NATO Secretary-General, brought down by a Belgian corruption scandal after a year in the job.
